sentence: No sooner had he sat down ___ the phone rang.
explanation: No sooner … than — fixed pair with inversion after 'no sooner'.

sentence: Hardly had we started ___ the engine failed.
explanation: Hardly … when — fixed pair: Hardly had we started when…

sentence: Never have I ___ such a stubborn refusal.
explanation: Inversion: Never have I + past participle — never adds emphasis.

sentence: Only after the third attempt ___ she pass the test.
explanation: 'Only after' at the front forces question word order: did she pass.

sentence: Not until the film ended ___ anybody speak.
explanation: Not until + time clause at the front: did anybody speak.

sentence: Little ___ they know that the deal had already collapsed.
explanation: Little did they know = they had no idea — emphatic idiom with inversion.

sentence: Rarely ___ this metro line run this late.
explanation: Rarely at the front: does + subject + infinitive.

sentence: Seldom have I been so ___ by a performance.
explanation: 'moved' — the audience was emotionally affected; inversion with have been.

sentence: No sooner ___ the contract been signed than problems arose.
explanation: Past perfect passive with inversion: had … been signed.

sentence: So convincing ___ his argument that nobody objected.
explanation: So + adjective at the front: was his argument that…

sentence: Such ___ the demand for tickets that the website crashed.
explanation: Such was the demand that… — emphatic result structure.

sentence: Should you ___ any problems, call reception immediately.
explanation: Should you experience… = If you experience… — formal conditional inversion.

sentence: ___ I known about the deadline, I would have hurried.
explanation: Had I known = If I had known — inversion replaces 'if'.

sentence: ___ it not been for your help, we would have failed.
explanation: Had it not been for = if it hadn't been for — fixed inverted conditional.

sentence: ___ I richer, I would travel the world.
explanation: Were I richer = If I were richer — formal inversion.

sentence: Only when the audit was complete ___ the accounts released.
explanation: Only when X happened were the accounts released — inversion after only when.

sentence: Not only ___ she apologise, she also paid for the damage.
explanation: Not only did she…, (but) she also… — inversion after not only.

sentence: Not only ___ the tickets expensive, but they were also sold out.
explanation: Not only were the tickets… — inversion with 'be' needs no auxiliary.

sentence: At no point ___ the pilot leave the cockpit.
explanation: At no point did… = never did… — negative adverbial inversion.

sentence: In no way ___ this report reflect the views of the editor.
explanation: In no way does this reflect… — formal disclaimer structure.

sentence: Only by practising daily ___ you improve your fluency.
explanation: Only by doing X will you… — future inversion after only by.

sentence: To such an extent ___ prices risen that buyers withdrew.
hint: To such an extent + past perfect
explanation: To such an extent had prices risen that… — emphatic result.

sentence: Come ___ it may, the trial must proceed.
explanation: 'Come what may' — fixed inverted idiom = whatever happens.

sentence: ___ as it may sound, the machine still works perfectly.
explanation: Adjective + as + subject + verb = although it sounds strange.

sentence: Try ___ she might, she couldn't restart the engine.
explanation: 'Try as somebody might' — fixed concessive inversion.

sentence: Barely ___ the survey published when the complaints arrived.
explanation: Barely had X happened when Y — like hardly… when.

sentence: Nowhere ___ the report mention the missing funds.
explanation: Nowhere does the report mention… — present simple inversion.

sentence: On no account ___ passengers open this door.
explanation: On no account should passengers… — formal prohibition.

sentence: Only in an emergency ___ this exit be used.
explanation: may + be + participle: this exit may be used only in an emergency.

sentence: Not since the 1990s ___ unemployment been so low.
explanation: Not since X has Y happened — present perfect inversion.

sentence: ___ the committee reach a decision, we cannot proceed.
explanation: Fronting 'Until…' emphasises the condition blocking progress.

sentence: So difficult ___ the exam that half the candidates failed.
explanation: So difficult was the exam that… — inversion for emphasis.

sentence: ___ you stands the man responsible for the discovery.
explanation: Dramatic inversion: 'Before you stands the man…' — the phrase of place is fronted and the verb precedes the subject.

sentence: Among the guests ___ the ambassador and her staff.
hint: fronted 'among' — verb agrees with later subject
explanation: Among the guests were the ambassador and her staff — verb before subject.

sentence: Also worth ___ is the museum's medieval wing.
explanation: Also worth noting is… — fronted comment structure.

sentence: Only after the interview ___ I realise how nervous I had been.
explanation: Only after X did I realise… — inversion.

sentence: Not once ___ the defendant change his statement.
explanation: Not once has he changed… — emphatic negative with present perfect.

sentence: Scarcely ___ the ink dried before the rumours started.
explanation: Scarcely had X happened before Y — like hardly… when.

sentence: So widespread ___ the outage that servers abroad noticed.
explanation: So widespread was the outage that… — inversion.

sentence: ___ the storm passed did the ferries resume service.
explanation: Only after/once the storm passed did… — fronted 'only' phrase.

sentence: To ___ did you address that complaint, exactly?
explanation: 'To whom…' — formal fronted preposition + whom.

sentence: Little ___ the chances of success be improved by patience.
explanation: Little will the chances be improved… — inversion with future.

sentence: Only when she apologised ___ he agree to meet again.
explanation: Only when she apologised did he agree — inversion.

sentence: Should the temperature ___ 40 degrees, the system shuts down.
explanation: Should the temperature exceed… = if it exceeds… — technical register.

sentence: Hardly had we left the house ___ it started to pour.
explanation: Hardly … when — fixed pair; 'than' belongs to 'no sooner'.

sentence: Scarcely had the plane taken ___ when the alarm sounded.
explanation: 'Taken off' completes the phrasal verb inside the inverted 'scarcely had … when' structure.

sentence: Not until the following morning ___ the damage reported to the police.
explanation: 'Not until + time' triggers inversion: 'was the damage reported'.

sentence: Only after the third reminder ___ she reply to my email.
explanation: 'Only after' fronts the condition, so 'did she reply' inverts.

sentence: Under no circumstances ___ the door be left unlocked.
explanation: 'Under no circumstances should/must the door be left unlocked' — modal + inversion.

sentence: No sooner ___ the contract been signed than the rumours started.
explanation: 'No sooner had … been signed than …' — past perfect with inversion.

sentence: Not only ___ the play cancelled, but the theatre was closed as well.
explanation: 'Not only was the play cancelled' — inverted passive.

sentence: Rarely ___ we seen such dedication from a new recruit.
explanation: 'Rarely have we seen' — inversion with present perfect, experience up to now.

sentence: Seldom does a debut novel ___ so much critical attention.
explanation: 'Seldom does a novel receive …' — the auxiliary 'does' carries tense; base verb follows.

sentence: Only when the results were published ___ the scale of the error become clear.
explanation: 'Only when … did the scale … become clear' — inverted past simple.

sentence: So convincing ___ her argument that even the sceptics agreed.
explanation: 'So convincing was her argument that …' — 'so + adj' fronted with inversion.

sentence: At no point ___ the passengers instructed to stay seated.
explanation: 'At no point were the passengers instructed …' — inverted passive.

sentence: Not since the winter of 1963 ___ temperatures dropped so low.
explanation: 'Not since 1963 have temperatures dropped …' — the only time from then until now.

sentence: Only by training every day ___ she hope to qualify.
explanation: 'Only by training every day could she hope …' — inverted modal.

sentence: ___ you require assistance, please do not hesitate to contact the desk.
explanation: 'Should you require …' = 'If you should require …' — formal inverted conditional.

sentence: ___ I known about the change of plan, I would have waited.
explanation: 'Had I known …' = 'If I had known …' — inverted third conditional.

sentence: Were it not ___ the funding cuts, the library would still be open.
hint: were it not ___ = if it were not for
explanation: 'Were it not for' introduces the one thing preventing the outcome.

sentence: ___ it not for your quick thinking, the whole project would have failed.
explanation: 'Were it not for …' = 'If it were not for …' — formal inverted conditional.

sentence: Hardly ___ anyone noticed the subtle change in the final scene.
explanation: 'Hardly has/had anyone noticed …' — inverted perfect.

sentence: Never ___ I expect to see my own name on the shortlist.
explanation: 'Never did I expect …' — inverted past simple.

sentence: Little did the suspects ___ that the police were listening.
explanation: 'Little did they know' — 'know' as bare verb after the inverted auxiliary 'did'.

sentence: Not until every passenger had been evacuated ___ the captain leave the ship.
explanation: 'Not until … did the captain leave …' — inverted past simple.

sentence: So rapid ___ the spread of the fire that the building was lost.
explanation: 'So rapid was the spread that …' — fronted 'so + adj' with inversion.

sentence: Nowhere ___ you find a better example of Gothic architecture.
explanation: 'Nowhere will you find …' — inverted future/modal.

sentence: Only later ___ we realise what he had done.
explanation: 'Only later did we realise' — inverted past simple.

sentence: Not once ___ she mentioned the incident to anyone.
explanation: 'Not once has she mentioned' — inversion with the perfect.

sentence: Never again ___ they offer credit to first-time customers.
explanation: 'Never again would they offer' — inverted modal for a past decision.

sentence: Barely ___ the ink dried when the complaints began to arrive.
explanation: 'Barely had the ink dried when …' — inverted past perfect.

sentence: Only after the audit ___ the missing funds come to light.
explanation: 'Only after the audit did the funds come to light'.

sentence: In no way ___ this decision reflect the views of the board.
explanation: 'In no way does this decision reflect …' — auxiliary 'does' + base verb.

sentence: On no account ___ personal data be shared with third parties.
explanation: 'On no account must/should data be shared' — modal + inversion.

sentence: So loud ___ the music that the neighbours called the police.
explanation: 'So loud was the music that …' — fronted 'so + adj' with inversion.

sentence: To such extremes ___ the fans go that the police were called in.
explanation: 'To such extremes did the fans go that …' — inverted past simple.

sentence: Only since the redesign ___ the app gained new users.
explanation: 'Only since the redesign has the app gained …' — perfect inversion.

sentence: ___ had I hung up than the phone rang again.
explanation: 'No sooner had I hung up than …' — the fixed inverted pair.

sentence: Not until the second edition ___ the book become a bestseller.
explanation: 'Not until the second edition did the book become …'.

sentence: Should the alarm ___, evacuate the building immediately.
explanation: 'Should the alarm sound' = 'If the alarm should sound' — base verb follows.'

sentence: ___ it not been for the lifeguard, the boy would have drowned.
explanation: 'Had it not been for …' = 'If it had not been for …'.

sentence: Little ___ the villagers suspect that the mine would ever reopen.
explanation: 'Little did the villagers suspect' — they had no idea.

sentence: Only by chance ___ the letters discovered decades later.
explanation: 'Only by chance were the letters discovered' — inverted passive.

sentence: Rarely ___ a debut film attracted such wide attention.
explanation: 'Rarely has a debut film attracted …' — perfect inversion.

sentence: Not only ___ the bridge unsafe, but it was also far too narrow.
explanation: 'Not only was the bridge unsafe' — inverted past simple of be.

sentence: Under no circumstances ___ refunds be given after this date.
explanation: 'Under no circumstances will refunds be given' — inverted modal passive.

sentence: At no time ___ the crew aware of the danger.
explanation: 'At no time was the crew aware' — inverted past simple of be.

sentence: Only when the last guest had left ___ she sit down.
explanation: 'Only when … had left did she sit down' — inverted past simple.

sentence: So convinced ___ he of his innocence that he refused the deal.
explanation: 'So convinced was he of …' — inversion after fronted 'so + adj'.
